ctx.x: Well, after he left Nat he went with his brother's group for a while, the Four Blazers. Johnny Moore's Four Blazers. But after that he just stopped. But he was a great guitarist, he was an innovator also. And let's see.

After Charlie I think Tal Farlow came through with bebop. Playing. And I think one of the great innovators of our time, and who was Wes Montgomery. Wes Montgomery in my estimation was one of the most lyrical guitarists I've ever heard. That includes everybody. He came closer to having it all as far as chords, as far as single strings, just -- he was just sheer beauty. Wes Montgomery.

Speaking of being fortunate to be around in this time, I'll have to go along with that, as far as he's concerned also, because he did something. I've heard guys with an awful lot of technique and everything, but the lines that Wes Montgomery played were the most interesting lines. And the -- his chord, just beautiful chords. He came closer to having it all, than anybody I know. And of course Joe Pass, what can I say. Joe Pass is also a great guitarist. He's a stylist. Yeah. But of the young crop I think we're…
